prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1048; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision reported at a signalized intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck from behind by a sedan, and the claimant reported a knee injury from the impact. The driver is named on the policy, so coverage is being confirmed on that basis.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision and records the other driver's account of the sequence.

Entry 3: Recorded statements taken from the other driver and two independent witnesses. All three describe the collision the same way as the initial report.

Entry 4: Scene photos and the vehicle damage photos received from the insured. Nothing in the photos suggests prior damage to the vehicle, and no earlier damage is known from the file.

Entry 5: Claimant is represented by counsel. Future contact is to go through the attorney's office. Medical authorization forms requested.

Entry 6: Claimant's recorded statement taken through counsel. The account is consistent with the original report, and some additional details were given that were not in the first notice of loss, but the core sequence did not change.

Entry 7: Medical records received. The reported knee injury fits the type and force of a rear impact of this kind. No prior treatment to the same body area appears in the records reviewed so far.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Records show improvement over time and the frequency of care tapered as the claimant recovered.

Entry 9: Repair estimate reviewed with the shop. Some of the listed damage may not be fully attributable to this impact, so the line items are being checked against the collision photos before a final figure is set.

Entry 10: Confirmed with the underwriting file that the policy was in force on the loss date and that nothing points to damage occurring before coverage began. Coverage position is unchanged.

Entry 11: Liability and injury evaluation sent to counsel for review. Next step is a response on the settlement demand within the timeframe set by the file.
